titre: Exercices — La modalité : déduction, reproche et regret (should have…)
consigne: Cherche chaque exercice au brouillon avant d'ouvrir le corrigé.

exercices.enonce: Choisis must, might ou can't : « His car isn't here, so he ___ be at home. »
corrige: Absence d'un indice attendu → conclusion sûre négative.
On emploie can't : he can't be at home.
exercices.reponse: He can't be at home.

exercices.enonce: Exprime une simple possibilité : « The door is unlocked. Someone ___ (to be) inside. »
corrige: Hypothèse non certaine → might/may/could.
Someone might be inside.
exercices.reponse: Someone might be inside. (may ou could sont aussi acceptés)

exercices.enonce: Transpose au passé : « He looks pale. He ___ (to see) a ghost! »
corrige: Déduction sûre sur un fait passé → must have + PP.
He must have seen a ghost!
exercices.reponse: He must have seen a ghost!

exercices.enonce: Exprime l'impossibilité passée : « You ___ (to finish) already — you only started five minutes ago! »
corrige: Certitude négative sur le passé → can't have + PP.
You can't have finished already.
exercices.reponse: You can't have finished already.

exercices.enonce: Formule un reproche : « The meeting was important, but Tom didn't come. → Tom ___ . »
corrige: Action attendue non faite → should have + PP.
Tom should have come.
exercices.reponse: Tom should have come.

exercices.enonce: Exprime un regret : « I told her the secret. Now I regret it. → I ___ . »
corrige: Action qu'on n'aurait pas dû faire → shouldn't have + PP.
I shouldn't have told her the secret.
exercices.reponse: I shouldn't have told her the secret.

exercices.enonce: Emploie needn't have : « I cooked a huge dinner, but nobody was hungry. → I ___ so much. »
corrige: Effort passé rendu inutile → needn't have + PP.
I needn't have cooked so much.
exercices.reponse: I needn't have cooked so much.

exercices.enonce: Complète avec mustn't ou don't have to : « Passengers ___ lean out of the window. » et « You ___ pay, it's on me. »
corrige: Interdiction → mustn't.
Absence d'obligation → don't have to.
exercices.reponse: Passengers mustn't lean out of the window. / You don't have to pay, it's on me.

exercices.enonce: Emploie could have : « The accident was avoided by luck. → Someone ___ (to be) killed. »
corrige: Conséquence grave possible mais non réalisée → could have + PP.
Someone could have been killed.
exercices.reponse: Someone could have been killed.

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Elle a dû rater son train ; elle aurait dû partir plus tôt. »
corrige: « a dû rater » = déduction passée → must have missed.
« aurait dû partir » = reproche → should have left.
exercices.reponse: She must have missed her train; she should have left earlier.

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Il doit être fatigué. » (déduction, pas obligation)
corrige: Déduction sûre sur le présent → must + BV.
He must be tired.
exercices.reponse: He must be tired.

exercices.enonce: Choisis must, might ou can't : « She has been working for twelve hours. She ___ be exhausted. »
corrige: Douze heures de travail : la conclusion est presque certaine.
Certitude positive → must.
exercices.reponse: She must be exhausted.

exercices.enonce: Choisis must, might ou can't : « That ___ be Paul on the phone — he is sitting right next to me! »
corrige: Paul est à côté de moi : c'est impossible que ce soit lui au téléphone.
Certitude négative → can't.
exercices.reponse: That can't be Paul on the phone.

exercices.enonce: Que signifie « You mustn't touch the paintings » : interdiction ou absence d'obligation ?
corrige: mustn't exprime l'interdiction.
L'absence d'obligation se dit don't have to.
exercices.reponse: Interdiction

exercices.enonce: Que signifie « You don't have to wear a tie » : interdiction ou absence d'obligation ?
corrige: don't have to = on n'est pas obligé.
Ce n'est pas interdit : on peut en porter une si on veut.
exercices.reponse: Absence d'obligation

exercices.enonce: Corrige la faute : « He mustn't be French — he doesn't understand a word of French. »
corrige: mustn't exprime l'interdiction, pas la certitude négative.
Certitude négative → can't.
exercices.reponse: He can't be French.

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Elle est peut-être chez elle. » (avec un modal)
corrige: Possibilité → may, might ou could + BV.
She might be at home.
exercices.reponse: She might be at home. (may ou could sont aussi acceptés)

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Il a dû rater le train. » (déduction)
corrige: « a dû » marque ici une déduction sur le passé → must have + PP.
miss → missed.
exercices.reponse: He must have missed the train.

exercices.enonce: Exprime une possibilité passée : « I can't find my keys. I ___ (to leave) them at the office. »
corrige: Hypothèse incertaine sur le passé → may/might/could have + PP.
leave → left.
exercices.reponse: I might have left them at the office. (may have ou could have sont aussi acceptés)

exercices.enonce: Transpose au passé : « They can't be at home. » → (yesterday) « They ___ at home yesterday. »
corrige: Impossibilité passée → can't have + PP.
be → been.
exercices.reponse: They can't have been at home yesterday.

exercices.enonce: Corrige la faute : « She mustn't have seen us — she walked past without saying hello. »
corrige: La certitude négative passée se dit can't have + PP, jamais mustn't have (mustn't = interdiction).
She can't have seen us.
exercices.reponse: She can't have seen us — she walked past without saying hello.

exercices.enonce: Formule un reproche : « You didn't revise for the test and you failed. → You ___ . »
corrige: Action attendue non faite → should have + PP.
revise → revised.
exercices.reponse: You should have revised for the test.

exercices.enonce: Corrige la faute d'orthographe : « You should of told me the truth. »
corrige: should of est une faute due à la prononciation de should've.
On écrit should have + PP.
exercices.reponse: You should have told me the truth.

exercices.enonce: Exprime un regret : « I ate three pieces of cake. Now I feel sick. → I ___ . »
corrige: Action qu'on n'aurait pas dû faire → shouldn't have + PP.
eat → eaten.
exercices.reponse: I shouldn't have eaten three pieces of cake.

exercices.enonce: Emploie needn't have : « I took a taxi to the station, but the train was two hours late. → I ___ a taxi. »
corrige: On a fait quelque chose d'inutile → needn't have + PP.
take → taken.
exercices.reponse: I needn't have taken a taxi.

exercices.enonce: Complète avec must ou have to : « In France, drivers ___ stop at a red light. » (règle imposée par la loi)
corrige: Contrainte extérieure (la loi) → have to.
Au pluriel : have to.
exercices.reponse: In France, drivers have to stop at a red light.

exercices.enonce: Complète avec mustn't ou don't have to : « It's Sunday tomorrow, so I ___ get up early. »
corrige: Le dimanche, rien n'oblige à se lever tôt.
Absence d'obligation → don't have to.
exercices.reponse: I don't have to get up early.

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Tu ne dois pas en parler à tes parents. » (c'est interdit)
corrige: Interdiction → mustn't + BV.
You mustn't tell your parents about it.
exercices.reponse: You mustn't tell your parents about it.

exercices.enonce: Formule un reproche avec could have : « You knew I was looking for a flat and you didn't tell me about yours. → You ___ ! »
corrige: Possibilité non réalisée, ton de reproche → could have + PP.
tell → told.
exercices.reponse: You could have told me!

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Il aurait pu se blesser. »
corrige: Conséquence possible mais non réalisée → could have + PP.
se blesser → hurt himself (participe passé : hurt).
exercices.reponse: He could have hurt himself.

exercices.enonce: Explique la différence : (a) « She might have won. » (b) « She could have won. » (on ne connaît pas le résultat dans (a) ; on sait qu'elle a perdu dans (b))
corrige: (a) might have + PP : hypothèse sur un passé inconnu (elle a peut-être gagné).
(b) could have + PP : possibilité non réalisée (elle aurait pu gagner, mais elle a perdu).
exercices.reponse: (a) elle a peut-être gagné ; (b) elle aurait pu gagner (mais n'a pas gagné).

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Vous auriez dû nous prévenir. »
corrige: « auriez dû » = reproche → should have + PP.
prévenir → warn (warned).
exercices.reponse: You should have warned us.

exercices.enonce: Réécris avec ought to : « You should have asked for permission. »
corrige: ought to have + PP est un synonyme plus formel de should have + PP.
On garde le participe passé asked.
exercices.reponse: You ought to have asked for permission.

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Je n'aurais pas dû lui mentir. »
corrige: Regret d'une action faite → shouldn't have + PP.
lie → lied (mentir).
exercices.reponse: I shouldn't have lied to him. (ou to her)

exercices.enonce: Corrige la faute : « You needn't have bring a present. »
corrige: needn't have est suivi du participe passé.
bring → brought.
exercices.reponse: You needn't have brought a present.

exercices.enonce: Choisis must have, might have ou can't have : « The streets are wet. It ___ rained during the night. »
corrige: Les rues mouillées sont un indice fort : déduction quasi certaine.
Certitude positive passée → must have + PP.
exercices.reponse: It must have rained during the night.

exercices.enonce: Choisis must have, might have ou can't have : « He ___ written this essay himself — he doesn't know any of these words. »
corrige: Il ne connaît aucun de ces mots : impossible qu'il ait écrit le texte.
Impossibilité passée → can't have + PP.
exercices.reponse: He can't have written this essay himself.

exercices.enonce: Associe chaque phrase à son sens (certitude positive, possibilité, certitude négative) : (a) « He might be ill. » (b) « He must be ill. » (c) « He can't be ill. »
corrige: must et can't expriment une certitude (positive ou négative).
might n'exprime qu'une possibilité.
exercices.reponse: (a) possibilité ; (b) certitude positive ; (c) certitude négative

exercices.enonce: Explique la différence : (a) « You needn't have paid. » (b) « You don't have to pay. »
corrige: (a) needn't have + PP : la personne a payé, mais c'était inutile (passé).
(b) don't have to : la personne n'est pas obligée de payer (présent ou futur).
exercices.reponse: (a) tu as payé, mais c'était inutile ; (b) tu n'es pas obligé de payer.

exercices.enonce: Transforme en regret avec should have : « I didn't listen to my teacher's advice. »
corrige: Ce qu'on n'a pas fait et qu'on regrette → should have + PP.
listen → listened.
exercices.reponse: I should have listened to my teacher's advice.

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Il ne peut pas avoir oublié : je le lui ai rappelé ce matin. »
corrige: « ne peut pas avoir oublié » = impossibilité passée → can't have forgotten.
« je le lui ai rappelé » → I reminded him.
exercices.reponse: He can't have forgotten: I reminded him this morning.

exercices.enonce: Traduis : « Tu n'étais pas obligé de venir, mais tu n'aurais pas dû partir si tôt. »
corrige: « n'étais pas obligé » → didn't have to (absence d'obligation au passé).
« n'aurais pas dû partir » → shouldn't have left.
exercices.reponse: You didn't have to come, but you shouldn't have left so early.

exercices.enonce: Complète : « Why did you walk home alone at night? Something terrible ___ (to happen) to you! »
corrige: Danger possible qui ne s'est pas réalisé → could have + PP.
happen → happened.
exercices.reponse: Something terrible could have happened to you!

exercices.enonce: Complète avec la forme qui convient du modal : « Look at all those people waiting. The film ___ be very popular. »
corrige: La file d'attente est un indice fort.
Déduction sûre au présent → must.
exercices.reponse: The film must be very popular.

exercices.enonce: Lis la situation : « Emma arrived at the airport at 9:50. Her flight left at 10:00. The doors closed at 9:40. » Écris une déduction passée et un reproche.
corrige: Déduction : elle est arrivée après la fermeture des portes → She must have missed her flight.
Reproche : She should have arrived earlier (ou should have left home earlier).
exercices.reponse: She must have missed her flight. / She should have arrived earlier. (Exemple de réponse)

exercices.enonce: Lis ce court dialogue : « — I bought the tickets online yesterday. — Oh no, entry was free! » Que peut-on dire ? Emploie needn't have puis could have.
corrige: Achat inutile → You needn't have bought the tickets.
Possibilité non réalisée → You could have saved your money.
exercices.reponse: You needn't have bought the tickets. / You could have saved your money. (Exemple de réponse pour la seconde phrase)

exercices.enonce: Lis la situation : « The window is broken. There is a football on the floor. The children were playing in the garden. » Écris une déduction sur le passé et un reproche aux enfants.
corrige: Déduction : The children must have broken the window with their ball.
Reproche : They shouldn't have played football so close to the house.
exercices.reponse: The children must have broken the window. / They shouldn't have played football so close to the house. (Exemple de réponse)

exercices.enonce: Repère et corrige les deux fautes : « You mustn't come tomorrow if you're tired, it's optional. And you should have call me last night. »
corrige: « it's optional » → absence d'obligation : don't have to, pas mustn't.
should have + participe passé : called.
exercices.reponse: You don't have to come tomorrow if you're tired, it's optional. And you should have called me last night.

exercices.enonce: Complète ce règlement de lycée avec must, mustn't ou don't have to : « Students ___ wear a uniform. They ___ use their phones in class. They ___ bring lunch: the canteen is open every day. »
corrige: Obligation imposée par le règlement → must.
Interdiction → mustn't ; pas d'obligation puisque la cantine est ouverte → don't have to.
exercices.reponse: Students must wear a uniform. They mustn't use their phones in class. They don't have to bring lunch.

exercices.enonce: Lis ce court texte : « Last summer, Jake spent all his savings on a new phone. In September, he couldn't afford the school trip to London. » Écris le regret de Jake à la première personne, avec shouldn't have puis avec should have.
corrige: Regret d'une action faite → I shouldn't have spent all my savings on a new phone.
Regret d'une action non faite → I should have saved some money for the trip.
exercices.reponse: I shouldn't have spent all my savings on a new phone. / I should have saved some money for the trip. (Exemple de réponse pour la seconde phrase)
